title: Amazon Associates & disclosure rule set — verified line by line against the official sources
how_to_read: Each row is one machine-checkable constraint. 'checked_by' names the automated guard in platform/ that enforces it. Rows are ordered as the policy document orders them.

rows.value: Free to join
rows.quote: The Associates Program is free to join

rows.value: None — Amazon authorises no paid set-up or consulting service for associates
rows.quote: We have never authorized any business to provide paid set-up or consulting services to our associates

rows.value: Original content, publicly available at the URL given in the application
rows.quote: Your Site(s) must contain original content and be publicly available via the website address provided in the application

rows.value: Only with significant commentary, analysis, or transformation
rows.quote: Original content utilizing third-party materials must contain significant commentary, analysis, or transformation

rows.claim: Amazon marks in domain, tag, Associates ID, or social username

rows.value: Prohibited for program participation

rows.value: 24 hours

groups.label: Catalog identifiers (needed before any product is trusted)

rows.value: A unique combination of 10 letters and numbers Amazon assigns to a product
rows.quote: an ASIN is a unique combination of 10 letters and numbers that Amazon assigns to a product—including product variations and product versions

rows.claim: Second official statement of the 10-character rule
rows.value: "a combination of 10 letters and numbers that Amazon assigns to a product"
rows.quote: An ASIN — short for “Amazon Standard Identification Number” — is a combination of 10 letters and numbers that Amazon assigns to a product

rows.value: Product variations and versions each get their own ASIN
rows.quote: Each product in the Amazon store is assigned a unique ASIN. That includes product variations, which are each assigned unique ASINs

rows.quote: The only exception is for books, which are identified using their ISBN number

groups.label: GitHub Pages publishing model for this site

rows.value: Deploy from a branch (root or /docs), or a custom Actions workflow
rows.quote: You can publish your site when changes are pushed to a specific branch, or you can write a GitHub Actions workflow to publish your site

rows.value: Root (/) of the source branch, or a /docs folder on that branch
rows.quote: the source folder can either be the root of the repository (/) on the source branch or a /docs folder on the source branch

rows.value: Branch main, path /, build_type legacy, status built
rows.quote: GET /repos/kanlerxz87-cyber/Zone1/pages -> build_type: legacy, source {branch: main, path: /}, status: built

rows.value: Public even if the repository is private
rows.quote: GitHub Pages sites are publicly available on the internet, even if the repository for the site is private

rows.value: Do not trigger a Pages build — so the site is built from committed files, not generated in CI and pushed back
rows.quote: Commits pushed by a GitHub Actions workflow that uses the GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger a GitHub Pages build
